title: Cost on the background, and the inertia of a body

key_results.statement: For every state and every $\lambda$, $L=\sum_hL_h+\sum_{\{h,h'\}}L_{hh'}$ with $L_{hh'}=0$ unless $\{h,h'\}$ is a cost edge; the site and edge costs do not depend on the placement of single-object terms, the common phase, the phase split or relabelling in $\bar A$.
Under $C\to C+c\mathbb 1$ with real $c$: $L_h\to L_h+c\,p_h$, $L_{hh'}\to L_{hh'}$ and $L\to L+c$; every edge cost is invariant and no single site cost is (unless $p_h=0$).

A real combination $\sum_h\alpha_hL_h+\sum\beta_{hh'}L_{hh'}$ whose coefficients may depend on the state is invariant under $C\to C+c\mathbb 1$ iff $\sum_h\alpha_hp_h=0$; examples are $L_h-p_hL$, $L_R-p_RL$ and $L_h/p_h-L_{h'}/p_{h'}$ (for $p_h,p_{h'}>0$).

For a set $R$ of places, $\mathrm dL_R/\mathrm d\lambda=\sum_{h\in R}\sum_{k\notin R}2\operatorname{Im}\langle\zeta^R_h\vert C_{hk}\vert\psi_k\rangle$ with $\lvert\zeta^R_h\rangle=\sum_{h'\in R}C_{hh'}\lvert\psi_{h'}\rangle$; each term contains exactly one boundary block, the interior blocks enter through $\zeta^R_h$, exterior blocks do not enter, and $L_R$ is constant if all boundary blocks vanish.

In the body-medium setting, for every $\lambda$, $a=\sum_{\{h,h'\}\in E}(A_{hh'}+B_{hh'})\Delta_{hh'}$ over the hopping edges, where $A_{hh'}$ contains only off-diagonal blocks and $B_{hh'}=2\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_h\vert C_{hh}C_{hh'}-C_{hh'}C_{h'h'}\vert\psi_{h'}\rangle$ contains the diagonal blocks; $a$ does not depend on the placement of single-object terms and is invariant under $C\to C+c\mathbb 1$.

With $a^{\mathrm{hop}}=\sum_EA_{hh'}\Delta_{hh'}$ and $a^{\mathrm{cost}}=\sum_EB_{hh'}\Delta_{hh'}$, $a=a^{\mathrm{hop}}+a^{\mathrm{cost}}$ and $B_{hh'}=L_{hh'}(\Omega_h-\Omega_{h'})+Z_{hh'}$ with the record term $Z_{hh'}=2\operatorname{Re}[t_{hh'}\langle\psi_h\vert\hat K_h-\hat K_{h'}\vert\psi_{h'}\rangle]$ and $\hat K_h=K_h-\epsilon_h$; the diagonal blocks enter explicitly only through the differences $C_{hh}-C_{h'h'}$ across hopping edges, and $A$, $L_{hh'}(\Omega_h-\Omega_{h'})$ and $Z$ are each invariant under $C\to C+c\mathbb 1$.

For the product start and arbitrary $\Omega_h$, $a(0)=a_0+\sum_{\{h,h'\}\in E}L_{hh'}(0)(\Omega_h-\Omega_{h'})\Delta_{hh'}$, where $a_0=\sum_E2\operatorname{Re}[t_{hh'}((\tau\phi)_h^*\phi_{h'}-\phi_h^*(\tau\phi)_{h'})]\Delta_{hh'}$ with $(\tau\phi)_h=\sum_{k\neq h}t_{hk}\phi_k$ is the value of $a(0)$ for equal $\Omega_h$ and does not depend on the diagonal entries $t_{hh}$.

For the product start and a uniform cost gradient, $a(0)=a_0+\mu F$ with $\mu=-\sum_{\{h,h'\}\in E}L_{hh'}(0)\,\Delta_{hh'}\,g(\Delta_{hh'},\cdot)$: the inertia is governed by the edge (hopping) costs of the body and the background differences, not by the site costs or by $L$; $\mu$ is $g$-symmetric and is positive semidefinite iff $\sum_EL_{hh'}(0)\,g(\Delta_{hh'},w)^2\le0$ for all $w$ (in particular if $L_{hh'}(0)\le0$ on every edge with $\Delta_{hh'}\neq0$).
For a localized start $\phi=\lvert\beta\rangle$ and all $\Omega_h$, $\mu=0$ and $a(0)=a_0=2\sum_h\lvert t_{h\beta}\rvert^2(u_h-u_\beta)=2w_2$, in agreement with (17.11)–(17.12).

For the chain, the site costs per unit weight are $\Omega_{h_m}=m\langle X\rangle$, which have a uniform gradient with force $F=-\langle X\rangle\,e/\sigma_X^2$ (fixed up to vectors $g$-orthogonal to $e$, which $\mu$ annihilates).
On the chain, $a^{\mathrm{hop}}(\lambda)\equiv0$ for every state, hence $a_0=0$ for every start.

For the chain and the start $2^{-1/2}(\lvert h_0\rangle+e^{i\theta}\lvert h_1\rangle)\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle$: $L_{h_0h_1}(0)=t\cos\theta$ (all other edge costs vanish), $\mu=-t\cos\theta\,e\,g(e,\cdot)$, $a_0=0$ and $a(0)=t\cos\theta\,\langle X\rangle\,e$, in agreement with the derivative of (17.22) at $\lambda=0$; $\mu$ is positive semidefinite iff $\cos\theta\le0$. For the start $\lvert h_0\rangle\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle$, $\mu=0$ and $a(0)=0$, in agreement with (17.19).

For the start of item 4(b) and $\lambda>0$: $a(\lambda)=t\sum_\xi w_\xi\,\xi\cos(\xi\lambda-\theta)\,e$ (the derivative of (17.22)), and with $\mu(\lambda)$ the expression (20.10) evaluated with the edge costs at $\lambda$, $a(\lambda)-\mu(\lambda)F=t\sum_\xi w_\xi(\xi-\langle X\rangle)\cos(\xi\lambda-\theta)\,e$; so $a(\lambda)=\mu(\lambda)F$ does not hold in general, the difference being $t\sigma_X^2\sin\theta\,\lambda\,e+O(\lambda^2)$ for small $\lambda$.

open_issues: The inverse inertia μ is defined at λ = 0 only; item 4(c) shows that its edge-cost extension μ(λ) misses the record term for λ > 0, and whether a convention-free inertia exists for λ > 0 is not addressed.
For general edge vectors (neither linearly independent nor collinear), positivity of μ is stated as positivity of the quadratic form in (20.10), not as a condition on single edge costs.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: with [C] = κ and [λ] = κ⁻¹, the background vectors, Ω and L scale as κ and the acceleration and μ as κ³; the terms of (20.9), (20.14), (20.15) and (20.5) are dimensionally consistent.

No hopping; equal records: without hopping there are no edges, so the acceleration and μ vanish and every region cost and every place weight is constant, as for a block-diagonal C; if all records are equal, all background vectors coincide, so the acceleration and μ vanish again.
Conservation of L: for R equal to the set of all places, (20.5) gives dL/dλ = 0; the shift check in Step 3 reproduces (20.3).
